checkpoints.title: Section 1 check
checkpoints.description: Show what you can do with the essentials — greetings, everyday words, and reading familiar French.

exercise.prompt: You arrive at a restaurant at 8 pm. What do you say?
You are leaving a shop. What do you say?
Someone holds the door open for you. You say:
Le chien est dans la rue.

options.text: The dog is in the street.
The cat is in the street.
The dog is at the station.
The dog is in the city.

checkpoints.title: Section 2 check
checkpoints.description: Show what you can do with the building blocks — articles, verbs, numbers and connected writing.

exercise.translation: I do not live in Lyon.

checkpoints.title: Section 3 check
checkpoints.description: Show what you can understand — listen to real announcements and dialogues, and read the messages, signs and short texts of everyday French.

exercise.question: When does the library close tonight?
What place is this announcement about?
Which platform does the Marseille train leave from?
How much does the museum entrance cost?
Which day is that price for?
When is the beach restaurant open?
When is Théo taking the train?

options.text: The café is next to the station

exercise.question: On which days is the library open?
What does the notice say about Sunday?
What does Camille buy in the morning?
How does Nora get to the library?

checkpoints.title: Section 4 check
checkpoints.description: Show what you can SAY — greet, introduce yourself, give real information and describe things aloud. The app grades the words it heard; it never scores your accent.

exercise.instruction: You walk into a restaurant at seven in the evening. Greet the waiter.
Someone holds the door open for you. Thank them.
You are leaving the shop after paying. Say goodbye.
Someone asks which language you speak. Answer: French.
Say that you like tea.
Say that you work in the evening.
Say how many dogs there are.
Say what it costs.
Say when the train leaves.
exercise.target: Le train part à dix heures
acceptedVariants: Le train part à dix heures

exercise.instruction: Say what this is.
Say what time of day this is.
Say that the shop is closed.

checkpoints.title: Section 5 check
checkpoints.description: Show what you can WRITE - introduce someone, write simple sentences, leave a short note and fill in a form. The app checks the information in your French; it never grades style.

exercise.instruction: You are Nadia. Introduce yourself in writing — name, age and city, in complete sentences.
modelAnswers: Je m'appelle Nadia, j'ai 35 ans et j'habite à Lyon.

exercise.instruction: You are Tom. Introduce yourself in writing — name, age and city, in complete sentences.
modelAnswers: Je m'appelle Tom, j'ai 28 ans et j'habite à Nice.

exercise.instruction: You are Emma. Introduce yourself in writing — name, age and city, in complete sentences.
modelAnswers: Je m'appelle Emma, j'ai 41 ans et j'habite à Marseille.

exercise.instruction: Write one sentence about Sofia: she likes tea.
Write one sentence: the cat drinks water.
Write about Léo in one or two short sentences: he lives in Paris and he works.
modelAnswers: Léo habite à Paris et il travaille.

exercise.instruction: Write a short note to Anna: greet her, and tell her the café is at three o'clock.

variants: le café est à trois heures

modelAnswers: Bonjour Anna, le café est à trois heures.

exercise.instruction: Write a short note: greet your friend, and say the train is Saturday at eight.

variants: le train est samedi à huit heures

modelAnswers: Salut, le train est samedi à huit heures.

exercise.instruction: Write a note: say hello, say you are at the library, and close with “see you tomorrow”.
modelAnswers: Bonjour, je suis à la bibliothèque. À demain !

exercise.instruction: Fill in the registration form with the details on the card.
Fill in the hotel form with the details on the card.
Fill in the library-card form with the details on the card.

checkpoints.title: Section 6 check
checkpoints.description: Show that you can TALK with someone - six short conversations with a patient partner. You will hear the partner (no written French) and answer by speaking. Asking to hear a line again, or more simply, never counts against you.
